findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed there is an accumulation of debris on the baffles of the ice machine. The PIC stated that the ice machine baffles were cleaned recently, however there is debris on the sides indicating that these spots were missed in the last cleaning. The inspector will follow-up on 12/1/2025 to check that the ice machine baffles have been cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed that an employee dumped ice into the hand washing sink during the inspection. The inspector educated the employee and PIC. Ensure that hand sinks are only used for hand washing. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The ceiling in the back room along the east wall is beginning to fall in. No foods are stored below however equipment and some single service items are stored nearby. Ensure that ceiling is repaired by the next routine inspection in 2024. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Person-in-charge was unaware of requirement for having a certified food manager certificate despite previous inspection requiring such certificate. Although no food was actively being prepared, PIC advised inspector that should a customer order a pizza, she would prepare it. Any time that food is available to order, a certified food manager must be present on site to oversee operations and ensure proper practices and procedures are followed. The facility currently has several violations including priority/priority foundation violations. This is a repeat violation from the inspection on 9/18/2021. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Upon arrival to the facility, inspector requested person in charge who was working behind the bar. PIC has a food handler certificate but does not have/cannot provide a certified food manager certificate upon request. Food is currently available to order and would be prepared by PIC if ordered. Any time that food is available to order, a certified food manager MUST be present. This is a repeat violation from 9/18/2021 but PIC states that she was not informed of this requirement during the previous inspection/spot check. PIC was shown previous inspection report. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Upon arrival to the facility, inspector observed ice in the hand washing sink behind the bar. Dumping is not allowed in hand washing sinks. Hand washing sinks are ONLY to be used for hand washing. Ensure that the hand washing sinks in the facility are used only to wash hands and never for dumping drinks, refuse or other materials. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the baffle of the ice machine had dark residue beginning to build up. There was enough residue that it could be easily wiped with a paper towel which then had black and red discoloration. Ice is considered a food and the baffle of the ice machine is a food contact surface. Ensure that surface is cleaned regularly to prevent the buildup of residue and microbial growths. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
When PIC was asked if sanitizer buckets were available for use, she advised that she had just dumped it and had not yet made a new one. Throughout the entire course of the inspection, sanitizer was not available to wipe surfaces. Ensure that sanitizer is available at all times and in the proper concentrations. Bleach is available for this and test strips are located behind the bar. Corrected on site by making up a sanitizer bucket, it was made at the correct concentration of approximately 200 ppm.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Wet wiping cloths were observed sitting atop the bar throughout the course of the inspection. In the kitchen, wet wiping cloths were found hanging from the faucet. Wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer when not actively being used to wipe surfaces. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
A pizza peel was observed to be rest on top of the pizza oven in the kitchen. The peel itself was slightly soiled and appeared to be actively in use today. The peel was sitting directly on top of heavily soiled equipment. Utensils used for the preparation or serving of food must be stored in a way which prevents contamination. Find a new location to store the peel or ensure the top of the pizza oven is cleaned, sanitized and free of debris. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the mop being stored in the bottom portion of the mop bucket. This is a repeat violation from 9/18/2021. Mops must be hung in manner which allows for air drying and prevents contamination. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements.

Bleach still incorrect - not for FOOD contact surfaces. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 9/23/21.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Observed no CFPM present during inspection. PIC does not have a food handler’s license and is cooking pizza. PIC was unaware of sanitizer needed for sani buckets, test strip availability. PIC was unaware of all paperwork needed for inspection purposes. Ensure staff is aware of practices, knowledge, and licenses needed for a food establishment. Inspector will follow-up on 9/28/21.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed no CFPM present during inspection. Employee lacked food handlers licensure, as well. A CFPM must be present during all operational hours when pizza is served. Ensure establishment has 2-3 CFPM’s in order to cover shifts.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements. Employee was unaware of document. Provided copy and further information related to employee health. Ensure all food handling employees sign document. Inspector will follow-up on 9/28/21.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy. Explained need for a policy and provided a copy. Facility is purchasing bleach to perform procedure. COS.

findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the dish machine to not be dispensing bleach as sanitizer. Inspector ran machine multiple times and tested - 0 ppm. Discussed servicing the machine. Inspector will follow-up on 9/20/21. Cease use of the dish machine and utilize the 3 compartment sink until repaired - wash, rinse, sanitize.

Observed no bleach at facility. Dish machine is not dispensing bleach. The 3 compartment sink is to be utilized until the dish machine is rectified. Bleach is being purchased by the night crew in order to utilize for 3 compartment sink and sani buckets. Discussed in length with PIC that the bleach must be for food contact surfaces, EPA registration number, and contain information about parts per million (ppm). Typically, bleach should test at 50 to 200 ppm to be actively sanitizing correctly. Inspector will follow-up on 9/20/21.

Observed no sani buckets present at facility; yet, wet, in-use rags present at bar. Discussed with PIC. Ensure wet rags are immersed in sanitizer when not in use. Ensure sani buckets have correct concentration of sanitizer. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Observed no bleach test strips. Facility has no way to test dish machine, sani buckets, or 3 compartment sink. Purchase bleach test strips and quaternary ammonium test strips (if utilizing). Inspector will follow-up on 9/28/21.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Observed mop to be stored within the mop bucket. Ensure mops are hung in a manner that allows to drip and/or air dry. Discussed with employee. COS.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

(REPEAT) Observed no food handler’s licenses available at the facility. PIC indicated she did not have a CFPM license and/or a food handler’s license. PIC was serving pizza. Ensure all staff has at minimum a food handler’s license unless a food protection manager. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 11/12/19.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed chest cooler (closest to handsink) to be soiled with water on bottom. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned as needed. Clean cooler. Reference 4-602.13.
